selection_criteria: The 80 most recently published GitHub-reviewed advisories for the pip ecosystem as of 2026-08-07, capped at 2 per source repository and 1 per fixing commit, restricted to those carrying a CWE and a fixing-commit reference into their own repository whose parent is not a merge, whose fix diff is under 400 KB, and which touch reviewable Python source outside tests and docs. Ground-truth spans are the lines the fix removed, excluding spans that are entirely imports, version bumps or comments. Two fixing commits were then excluded by hand as bulk refactors whose spans mark remediation plumbing rather than the defect; the reasons are in benchmark/corpus/labelled-excluded.txt. NOT filtered by CWE: classes no 3a detector can emit are retained and reported as a stratum. Newest-first sampling makes the set post-cutoff for any model evaluated later.

pymdown-extensions: exponential-backtracking ReDoS in caret, tilde, betterem, and magiclink inline processors

findings.title: Regex change introduces catastrophic backtracking potential

evidence.why: The diff replaces a single-char-per-iteration alternation `(?:[-\w]|\.(?!=$))*` with `[-\w]*(?:\.[-\w.]+)*`, where the inner `[-\w.]+` and outer `*` both match dots/word chars ambiguously; on crafted input like many dots with no terminating boundary this can cause exponential backtracking (ReDoS) when matching untrusted text.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Removed negative lookahead widens backtracking in nested quantifier

evidence.why: Changing `\*{2,}(?!\*)` to `\*{2,}` inside a `(?:...)+?` group removes a constraint that previously limited ambiguous matches of runs of asterisks, increasing backtracking paths when processing untrusted markdown with long asterisk runs.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

findings.title: Namespace prefix search uses unescaped LIKE pattern

evidence.why: ns_condition now builds `store.prefix LIKE %s` with `_namespace_to_text(op.namespace_prefix)` directly interpolated as a LIKE pattern with no escaping of `%`/`_` and no segment-boundary anchoring (removed `_namespace_prefix_condition`/`_escape_like_literal`), so a namespace label containing `%` or `_` is treated as a wildcard and a prefix like `("foo",)` now also matches `("foobar",)`, letting a caller read data outside their intended namespace scope.

remediation.summary: Use parameter binding; never build SQL by string interpolation.

findings.title: list_namespaces prefix/suffix match uses unescaped, unanchored LIKE

evidence.why: The diff replaces the segment-anchored regex (`prefix ~ %s` with escaped, `[^.]+`-based pattern) with plain `prefix LIKE %s` fed `_namespace_to_text(condition.path, handle_wildcards=True)` + `%`/`%`+pattern; labels containing literal `%`/`_` now act as SQL wildcards and matches are no longer anchored to `.` segment boundaries, allowing unintended cross-namespace matches (e.g. prefix `foo` matching `foobar`).

remediation.summary: Use parameter binding; never build SQL by string interpolation.

findings.title: SQLite namespace_prefix search uses unescaped, unanchored LIKE

evidence.why: Replaces the `_namespace_prefix_condition` (GLOB with escaped metacharacters and segment anchoring) with a bare `s.prefix LIKE ?` over `_namespace_to_text(op.namespace_prefix)+'%'`; since SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive and `%`/`_` in a namespace label are now live wildcards, prefix scoping no longer isolates namespaces (e.g. tenant `foo` search also returns `Foobar`).

remediation.summary: Use parameter binding; never build SQL by string interpolation.

findings.title: SQLite list_namespaces prefix/suffix match uses unescaped LIKE, drops segment anchoring

evidence.why: Removes the `_namespace_match_pattern`/regex-based `NS_MATCH_FUNCTION` segment-boundary matching and replaces it with `prefix LIKE ?` on `_namespace_to_text(cond.path, handle_wildcards=True)`, so labels with literal `%`/`_` are treated as wildcards and matches are not anchored to `.` boundaries, letting e.g. a prefix `uid.a` unintentionally match `uid.ab...`.

remediation.summary: Use parameter binding; never build SQL by string interpolation.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Upgrade now happens before request body is consumed, enabling request smuggling

evidence.why: The diff removes the deferred `_pending_upgrade` mechanism and instead sets `_upgraded = True` immediately in on_headers_complete, then cb_on_headers_complete returns 2 to stop parsing as soon as headers complete. Any Content-Length/chunked body bytes on the upgrade request are no longer read by the parser and are instead handed back as the 'tail' (post-upgrade data), so if the application declines the upgrade and continues on the same HTTP connection, the unread body bytes are misinterpreted as the start of a subsequent request/response, allowing request smuggling.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Python parser also drops deferred-upgrade body handling, exposing body bytes as protocol tail

evidence.why: self._upgraded is now set immediately from msg.upgrade and the payload StreamReader is skipped whenever `not self._upgraded`, so a request/response with Connection: Upgrade and a body no longer has its body read into a payload; instead the parser stops and the unread body is returned as tail data, which can be misinterpreted by callers that decline the upgrade, enabling desynchronization/smuggling between the declining handler and the next parsed message.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Path confinement check reverts to lexical-only, bypassable via symlinks/absolute paths

evidence.why: The diff removes root/candidate .resolve() (no symlink resolution) and replaces relative_to() containment with os.path.relpath()+startswith('..'), which can be defeated by symlinks or path components like 'foo../bar' evading the '..' prefix check; combined with removal of the skip-on-None-rel_path guard below, this reintroduces the arbitrary file read CWE-22/CWE-200 that this PR reverts.

findings.title: Files outside working directory are no longer skipped, only renamed

findings.title: Path traversal via percent-encoding decoded after boundary check

evidence.why: file_path is built and checked with startswith before any unquote() call; unquote only happens later on the exists() fallback, and the original commonpath-based _inside_root_path safeguard was removed in favor of a naive startswith, which also lets a sibling directory sharing the root as a string prefix (e.g. /images-sibling) pass the check.

findings.title: Unquoted fallback path used without re-validating root boundary

evidence.why: when the initial exists(file_path) fails, file_path = unquote(file_path) decodes percent-encoded traversal sequences like %2e%2e into '..' and the result is used directly without re-running the inside_root_path check or re-applying abspath, allowing escape outside FILE_LOADER_ROOT_PATH.

remediation.summary: Resolve the path and verify it stays inside the intended root.

`proot-distro install` has a Symlink Escape (Arbitrary Host File Write) via Malicious Tar Archive

findings.title: Symlink-through-parent path traversal reintroduced in tar extraction

evidence.why: The diff removes _safe_resolve clamping and replaces it with plain os.path.join(rootfs_dir, *rel_parts[:-1]); a crafted archive member creating a symlink (e.g. evil -> /) followed by a member named evil/passwd will now be written through that symlink onto the host filesystem, escaping rootfs_dir.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Hard-link source/dest no longer clamped inside rootfs

evidence.why: _defer_hardlink now computes dest/link_src with plain os.path.join instead of _safe_resolve, so a symlink planted earlier by the same archive can redirect the deferred hardlink copy's read or write outside rootfs_dir, letting an attacker copy host files into the archive or overwrite host files via copy2.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Deferred hard-link copy loop no longer re-resolves endpoints

evidence.why: The loop now directly uses the (dest, src) tuples stored without clamped resolution, so a symlink planted by a later member between queue-time and copy-time can redirect shutil.copy2's source or destination outside rootfs_dir.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Directory member no longer removes pre-existing symlink before makedirs

evidence.why: The removed `if os.path.islink(dest): _remove_fstree(dest)` check meant os.makedirs/chmod/utime now can act through a symlink planted by an earlier member at the same path, escaping rootfs_dir.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: COPY/ADD build step file materialisation loses symlink clamping

evidence.why: host is now built with plain os.path.join(rootfs_dir, arcname.lstrip('/')) instead of _safe_resolve, so a crafted layer/ADD tar with a symlink component can redirect writes outside rootfs_dir during image build.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Restore command no longer clamps destination through _safe_dest

evidence.why: The removal of the `dest = _safe_dest(...)` call means a symlink planted earlier in the same backup archive can redirect subsequent member writes (including via the hardlink path using unresolved link_src) outside the container directory during restore.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Security policy fails open when read-operations index fails to load

evidence.why: main() now catches the exception from get_read_only_operations(), logs a warning, and sets READ_OPERATIONS_INDEX = None instead of raising; the server continues to start and serve requests with the denylist/elicit policy effectively disabled for the process lifetime.
